title: He built something no one would question.
paragraphs:
He built something no one would question.
And that was the problem.

Because the most dangerous sin…
is the one that looks successful.

Shebna wasn’t weak.
He was influential. Positioned. Trusted.

But while a nation stood on the edge of collapse…
he was busy securing his legacy.

Isaiah records it with surgical precision—God confronts him: “What have you to do here… that you have cut out here a tomb for yourself?” (Isaiah 22:16).
A monument.
A name etched in stone.
A life built to be remembered.
But not by God.
And here’s the open wound most won’t touch:

You can be active in God’s house…
and still be building your own.

Serving—but seen.
Giving—but noticed.
Leading—but secretly craving applause.

Not because you’re evil.
But because something inside you still wants to be exalted.
Read that again.

This isn’t just Shebna’s story.
This is the quiet war inside people who love God… but still love recognition.

The applause you didn’t admit you needed.
The obedience you delayed because it wouldn’t be seen.
The “yes” you gave publicly… but wrestled with privately.
And no one knows.
Except God.

Because Scripture says in Proverbs 16:18, “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.”
Not after. Before.

Meaning—your fall doesn’t start when you collapse.
It starts when you crown yourself.
AHA REVELATION:

Pride doesn’t always shout.
Sometimes it whispers, “You deserve this.”
And that whisper builds tombs.

Shebna wasn’t judged for laziness.
He was judged for self-exaltation.

God says in Isaiah 22:19, “I will thrust you from your office… you will be pulled down.”
Not because he had no role—
but because he forgot who gave it.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

Are you building something for God…
or building something out of God?
Sit with that.

Because some of us don’t need more opportunities.
We need purification.

There are prayers you’ve been praying…
that God is delaying—not because He’s silent,
but because your heart isn’t ready to carry what you’re asking for.
That’s mercy.
Because unchecked pride can turn blessings into idols.
And here’s the piercing truth:
God will remove what you misuse.

Even if it’s ministry.
Even if it’s influence.
Even if it’s something you once received from Him.

That’s not cruelty.
That’s holiness.
But here’s where grace breaks in.
Because the story doesn’t end with removal.
Right after Shebna… God raises Eliakim. A faithful servant. And then Scripture keeps unfolding until we meet Jesus—the true and better One.

Where Shebna built a tomb for himself…
Jesus walked toward a tomb for us.

Where Shebna tried to secure his name…
Jesus emptied Himself, “taking the form of a servant… humbling Himself to death—even death on a cross” (Philippians 2:7–8).
And here’s the Gospel:
We have all been Shebna.

Romans 3:23 says “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
Every hidden motive.
Every quiet pride.
Every moment we wanted the glory that belongs to Him.
But God didn’t just expose our pride.
He paid for it.
On the cross, Jesus took the weight of our self-exaltation… and offered us something we could never build:
Grace.
Ephesians 2:8–9 makes it clear—“by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.”

No monuments.
No self-made identity.
No earned glory.
Just mercy.
This is your turning point.

Not to try harder.
Not to perform better.
But to surrender deeper.

Lay down the need to be seen.
Lay down the craving for recognition.
Lay down the subtle pride that dresses itself as calling.
Because you were not created to build your name.
You were created to carry His.
Identity shift:

You are not the architect of your own glory.
You are a vessel of His grace.

And vessels don’t boast.
They overflow.
So come back.
Quietly. Honestly.
Repent—not just of sin… but of self.
Let Jesus take the throne you’ve been slowly reclaiming.

Because the safest place in the world…
is not at the top.
It’s surrendered.
If this is hitting deeper than expected, stay a little longer.

And something else is coming next…
because Shebna is not the only one we’ve overlooked.
Someone close to you is fighting a silent version of this.
